     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU

     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258	
     259	```
     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     273	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     274	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     275	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     276	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     277	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     278	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     279	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     280	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     281	      zero or as healthy.
     282	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     283	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     284	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     285	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     286	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     287	      the one you blamed.
     288	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     289	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     290	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     291	
     292	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     293	
     294	## Success criteria
     295	
     296	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     297	  proven coverage.
     298	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     299	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     300	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     301	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     302	- No mutating API call was made.

{"id": "3c932adc-c23c-43f7-9822-b03a25f89931", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"thinking": "This is a training throughput slowdown investigation on a GPU cluster reading from FSx for Lustre in us-west-2, and I need to determine whether storage, network, or GPUs are to blame. Since the user mentioned "last few days" without a specific window, I'll frame this as an incident investigation covering the last 72 hours.

I'm scoping this to account 111122223333, region us-west-2, with the FSx filesystem fs-077c776983688ad76, and I still need to figure out what compute platform is running the training (HyperPod, ParallelCluster, EKS, or raw EC2). fundamental, actionable root cause: the GPU compute fleet for ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 was statically bound to a single fixed-duration EC2 Capacity Block (cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b, purchased 2026-09-22T19:28:13Z, extended 2026-09-24T02:35:17Z to end 2026-09-27T11:30:00Z). Confirm current capacity state and baseline config","children":[]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_pre-validate__body","type":"accordion-content","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_pre-validate__md","type":"markdown","props":{},"text":"*Confirm no existing active/scheduled reservation is available before purchasing new capacity*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 describe-capacity-reservations --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p6-b200.48xlarge Name=state,Values=active,scheduled,payment-pending --region us-west-2\n```\n\n*Discover available Capacity Block purchase offerings matching the fleet shape*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 describe-capacity-block-offerings --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-count 2 --capacity-duration-hours 48 --region us-west-2\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- No offerings may be available for this exact shape — vary instance count/duration/start date or use the On-Demand fallback\n\n*Record the current launch template versions as rollback baseline before any config change*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --versions '$Latest' '$Default' --region us-west-2\n```","children":[]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply","type":"accordion-item","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__trg","type":"accordion-trigger","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__row","type":"container","props":{"layout":"horizontal"},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__phase","type":"badge","props":{"variant":"secondary"},"text":"apply","children":[]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__label","type":"text","props":{},"text":"2. Acquire new capacity and rebind the cluster","children":[]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__body","type":"accordion-content","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_apply__md","type":"markdown","props":{},"text":"*Acquire a new Capacity Block to replace the deleted cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 purchase-capacity-block --capacity-block-offering-id <OFFERING_ID> --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --region us-west-2\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- Purchasing a Capacity Block commits a non-refundable upfront charge for the full duration\n- If no Capacity Block offering is available, fall back to an On-Demand Capacity Reservation\n\n*Fallback: create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation if no Capacity Block offering is available*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 create-capacity-reservation --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --availability-zone <AZ> --instance-count <COUNT> --end-date-type limited --end-date <RUN_END> --region us-west-2  # fallback only\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- On-Demand reservations bill for the full reserved window whether or not instances run\n\n*Stop the compute fleet before changing the capacity binding*\n\n```bash\npcluster update-compute-fleet --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --status STOP_REQUESTED --region us-west-2\n```\n\n*Rebind the cluster's compute resource to the new, active capacity through the authoritative ParallelCluster config*\n\nEdit the ParallelCluster configuration YAML so the compute resource's CapacityReservationTarget.CapacityReservationId points to the new reservation ID, keeping CapacityType consistent with the reservation type used. Do not hand-edit the launch template directly — ParallelCluster manages and would overwrite it.\n\n*Apply the rebind so slurm_resume/clustermgtd will relaunch GPU nodes against the new capacity*\n\n```bash\npcluster update-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --cluster-configuration <updated-config.yaml> --region us-west-2\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- A malformed config can leave the cluster in UPDATE_FAILED\n\n*Re-enable the compute fleet so Slurm scales GPU nodes back up and resumes training from checkpoint*\n\n```bash\npcluster update-compute-fleet --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --status START_REQUESTED --region us-west-2\n```","children":[]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_post-validate","type":"accordion-item","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_post-validate__trg","type":"accordion-trigger","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_post-validate__row","type":"container","props":{"layout":"horizontal"},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_post-validate__phase","type":"badge","props":{"variant":"secondary"},"text":"post validate","children":[]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_post-validate__label","type":"text","props":{},"text":"3. Revert configuration if the rebind fails","children":[]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_rollback__body","type":"accordion-content","props":{},"text":null,"children":[{"id":"mitigation-plan__step_rollback__md","type":"markdown","props":{},"text":"*Revert the ParallelCluster configuration to the pre-change baseline if the rebind causes update failures*\n\nRe-run pcluster update-cluster with the prior configuration (restored from the pre_validate baseline) and confirm the stack returns to UPDATE_COMPLETE.\n\n*Cancel a newly created On-Demand Capacity Reservation if created in error*\n\n```bash\naws ec2 cancel-capacity-reservation --capacity-reservation-id <NEW_CR_ID> --region us-west-2  # only if an On-Demand reservation was created in error\n```\n\n**Risks:**\n- This applies only to On-Demand Capacity Reservations — purchased Capacity Blocks are non-refundable and cannot be cancelled","children":[]}]}]}]},{"id":"mitigation-plan__ccs","type":"markdown","props":{},"text":"### Code change specification\n\n**1. Prevent recurrence of GPU capacity withdrawal by renewing/replacing the Capacity Block before it ends and binding the fleet to a valid reservation through infrastructure-as-code**\n\nThe IaC for distributed-training-triage-b200 statically binds the compute resource to a single fixed-duration Capacity Block; when it ended it was not renewed, leaving no valid capacity to relaunch into. Parameterize the capacity reservation ID in IaC and document a renewal runbook.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Capacity reservation ID is parameterized in IaC rather than hard-coded\n- A documented runbook exists to acquire and rebind a replacement block before expiry\n- Configuration no longer references the deleted reservations cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b or cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5\n\n**2. Add proactive alerting on Capacity Block expiry**\n\nNo EventBridge rule currently alerts on the 'Capacity Block Expiration Warning' event for this fleet. Add one with enough lead time to acquire and rebind replacement capacity before instances begin terminating.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- An EventBridge rule matches the EC2 'Capacity Block Expiration Warning' event and notifies operators\n- Lead time is sufficient to rebind before the 30-minute pre-termination window","children":[]}]}]}]}}

Parameterize the capacity reservation ID in IaC and document a renewal runbook.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- Capacity reservation ID is parameterized in IaC rather than hard-coded\n- A documented runbook exists to acquire and rebind a replacement block before expiry\n- Configuration no longer references the deleted reservations cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b or cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5\n\n**2. Add proactive alerting on Capacity Block expiry**\n\nNo EventBridge rule currently alerts on the 'Capacity Block Expiration Warning' event for this fleet. Add one with enough lead time to acquire and rebind replacement capacity before instances begin terminating.\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- An EventBridge rule matches the EC2 'Capacity Block Expiration Warning' event and notifies operators\n- Lead time is sufficient to rebind before the 30-minute pre-termination window","children":[]}]}]}]}}

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### GPU training compute fleet never launched / zero throughput
**Description:** GPU training on ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 (2x p6-b200.48xlarge, 8xB200 each) is fully stalled, not merely slowed: zero compute nodes have run since the EC2 Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b was reclaimed at ~2026-09-27T11:00:00Z UTC. Prior to that, the fleet ran healthy from ~2026-09-23T16:24Z, reading data from FSx (3 client connections, a 90.88GB read burst on 2026-09-24). Since the reclamation, every slurm_resume relaunch attempt has failed with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active', and only the head node remains running. FSx storage, EFA/NCCL networking, and GPU hardware (kernel logs showing zero Xid/ECC/NVLink-fatal errors across the full healthy window) were all confirmed healthy — the stall is caused entirely by the loss of GPU compute capacity, not a performance degradation or hardware fault.
**Time:** 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Compute fleet launches failed: inactive Capacity Reservation
**Description:** clustermgtd/slurm_resume on the head node (i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8) attempted RunInstances for p6-b200.48xlarge compute nodes via launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 three times on 2026-09-27 (11:17:33Z, 11:18:33Z, 11:19:33Z), each failing with 'Client.InvalidParameterValue: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active.' No compute nodes launched successfully at any point in the incident window 2026-09-28T04:08Z→2026-10-01T04:08Z. The reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is now not found (deleted).
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-stall

### Root Cause: No Capacity Block renewal/expiry alerting process
**Description:** The fundamental, actionable root cause: the GPU compute fleet for ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 was statically bound to a single fixed-duration EC2 Capacity Block (cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b, purchased 2026-09-22T19:28:13Z, extended 2026-09-24T02:35:17Z to end 2026-09-27T11:30:00Z). No process existed to renew or replace this block ahead of its expiry, and no EventBridge alert was configured to warn operators of the approaching end time. When the block's extended end time arrived, EC2 reclaimed the two p6-b200.48xlarge compute nodes (beginning ~30 minutes before expiry, consistent with Capacity Block termination behavior), and every subsequent relaunch attempt by the cluster's slurm_resume/clustermgtd role failed because the reservation was no longer active and no replacement capacity existed. This is the fundamental cause other causes cascade from: fixing it (parameterizing the reservation ID in IaC and adding expiry alerting, plus acquiring replacement capacity) is what would prevent recurrence.
**Cascades to:** finding-capacity-reservation-inactive

### Hypothesis: FSx Lustre storage bottleneck
**Description:** Hypothesis raised because the FSx Lustre file system fs-077c776983688ad76 is SCRATCH_2 with only 1,200 GiB (≈234 MB/s aggregate ceiling), which looked undersized for B200 training I/O.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-stall

#### Gaps
- **No CI/CD or git integration for training code:** No repositories are connected to this environment, so a training-side config regression (batch size, dataloader workers, NCCL/EFA env vars, FSx mount options) cannot be ruled out purely from infra signals — though it is now moot given the compute fleet never launched at all.
- **Capacity Block interruption/NCCL transport not observable:** Per-instance EventBridge 'Capacity Block Interruption Warning' events were not routed to any retained target, so direct per-instance corroboration of the exact reclamation trigger is unavailable (the reclaim timing was instead inferred from the kernel logs stopping precisely at 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z and the CloudTrail-confirmed Capacity Block extension end date of 11:30:00Z). Additionally, NCCL transport logs were absent from the kernel log source, so NCCL/TCP-fallback behavior during the healthy run window could not be directly observed. Neither gap affects the proven root cause (Capacity Block expiry), but they limit the depth of direct instance-level evidence available.

### Hypothesis: EFA/NCCL network bottleneck
**Description:** Hypothesis raised because the ParallelCluster head node i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8 carries the tag parallelcluster:networking=EFA=NONE, suggesting a possible EFA/NCCL network transport gap for distributed training.
**Cascades to:** symptom-training-stall

#### Gaps
- **No CI/CD or git integration for training code:** No repositories are connected to this environment, so a training-side config regression (batch size, dataloader workers, NCCL/EFA env vars, FSx mount options) cannot be ruled out purely from infra signals — though it is now moot given the compute fleet never launched at all.
- **Capacity Block interruption/NCCL transport not observable:** Per-instance EventBridge 'Capacity Block Interruption Warning' events were not routed to any retained target, so direct per-instance corroboration of the exact reclamation trigger is unavailable (the reclaim timing was instead inferred from the kernel logs stopping precisely at 2026-09-27T11:00:00Z and the CloudTrail-confirmed Capacity Block extension end date of 11:30:00Z). Additionally, NCCL transport logs were absent from the kernel log source, so NCCL/TCP-fallback behavior during the healthy run window could not be directly observed. Neither gap affects the proven root cause (Capacity Block expiry), but they limit the depth of direct instance-level evidence available.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Restore GPU training capacity for AWS ParallelCluster distributed-training-triage-b200 by acquiring a new EC2 Capacity Block (or On-Demand Capacity Reservation) for p6-b200.48xlarge in us-west-2, rebinding the cluster's compute resource to the new reservation ID through the ParallelCluster configuration, then restarting the compute fleet so Slurm auto-resume relaunches the GPU nodes and the job resumes from its latest checkpoint.

## Reasoning
The compute fleet's EC2 Capacity Block cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b ended and went inactive around 2026-09-27 11:00-12:00 UTC, so the p6-b200.48xlarge GPU nodes were reclaimed and every relaunch attempt since has failed with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active'. Current-state checks confirm cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is deleted, the launch template's alternate reference cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 is also deleted, and no active/scheduled/payment-pending capacity reservation exists for p6-b200.48xlarge in the account. A Capacity Block extension is impossible once the reservation is deleted — the only path is to acquire new capacity and rebind the fleet. FSx and EFA networking were ruled healthy and are left unchanged.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Pre Validate

#### 1.1 Confirm no existing active/scheduled reservation is available before…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-reservations --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p6-b200.48xlarge Name=state,Values=active,scheduled,payment-pending --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm no existing active/scheduled reservation is available before purchasing new capacity

#### 1.2 Discover available Capacity Block purchase offerings matching the fleet…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-block-offerings --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-count 2 --capacity-duration-hours 48 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Discover available Capacity Block purchase offerings matching the fleet shape
**Risks:** No offerings may be available for this exact shape — vary instance count/duration/start date or use the On-Demand fallback

#### 1.3 Record the current launch template versions as rollback baseline before…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-id lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 --versions '$Latest' '$Default' --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Record the current launch template versions as rollback baseline before any config change

### Step 2: Apply

#### 2.1 Acquire a new Capacity Block to replace the deleted cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 purchase-capacity-block --capacity-block-offering-id <OFFERING_ID> --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Acquire a new Capacity Block to replace the deleted cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b
**Risks:** Purchasing a Capacity Block commits a non-refundable upfront charge for the full duration, If no Capacity Block offering is available, fall back to an On-Demand Capacity Reservation

#### 2.2 Fallback: create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation if no Capacity Block…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 create-capacity-reservation --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --availability-zone <AZ> --instance-count <COUNT> --end-date-type limited --end-date <RUN_END> --region us-west-2  # fallback only
```
**Purpose:** Fallback: create an On-Demand Capacity Reservation if no Capacity Block offering is available
**Risks:** On-Demand reservations bill for the full reserved window whether or not instances run

#### 2.3 Stop the compute fleet before changing the capacity binding
**Type:** command
```
pcluster update-compute-fleet --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --status STOP_REQUESTED --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Stop the compute fleet before changing the capacity binding

#### 2.4 Rebind the cluster's compute resource to the new, active capacity…
**Type:** text
Edit the ParallelCluster configuration YAML so the compute resource's CapacityReservationTarget.CapacityReservationId points to the new reservation ID, keeping CapacityType consistent with the reservation type used. Do not hand-edit the launch template directly — ParallelCluster manages and would overwrite it.
**Purpose:** Rebind the cluster's compute resource to the new, active capacity through the authoritative ParallelCluster config

#### 2.5 Apply the rebind so slurm_resume/clustermgtd will relaunch GPU nodes…
**Type:** command
```
pcluster update-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --cluster-configuration <updated-config.yaml> --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Apply the rebind so slurm_resume/clustermgtd will relaunch GPU nodes against the new capacity
**Risks:** A malformed config can leave the cluster in UPDATE_FAILED

#### 2.6 Re-enable the compute fleet so Slurm scales GPU nodes back up and…

     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |
     32	| `MetadataOperations` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Sharp rise aligned with the slowdown | Metadata-heavy workload |
     33	| `FreeDataStorageCapacity` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Minimum per OST | Any OST < 10% free while others have space | Imbalanced striping, write failures possible |

{"id": "dc44bde0-dccf-48e3-bc93-a7d022837637", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_2n8seXpxawZAeNF1dIlZEx", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.
     233	
     234	**Work the core first, then extend.** All sixteen checks together cost more tool calls than
     235	a single answer usually has room for, and a readiness question with no verdict is a failed
     236	answer however much evidence sits behind it (see R1). So run them in two passes.
     237	
     238	The core, which decides whether the run can start at all:
     239	
     240	| Check | Question it settles |
     241	|-------|---------------------|
     242	| P1 | Does the Capacity Block or training plan outlast the run? |
     243	| P2 | Is there an extension, if it does not? |
     244	| P3 | Is there a spare node to replace a failure? |
     245	| P4 | Is `NodeRecovery` on? |
     246	| P5 | Are deep health checks enabled? |
     247	| P6 | Is GPU error logging arriving, so a failure during the run is visible? |
     248	
     249	Write the readiness verdict as soon as those six are scored. P7 to P16 then refine it, and
     250	each one you reach can only add a `RISK`, never change a `FAIL` already found in the core.
     251	Anything you do not reach is reported `Not checked` with the call that would settle it, which
     252	is an honest answer; silence is not. If the core itself is incomplete, say which part and
     253	give the verdict you can support.
     254	
     255	## Step 6: Report
     256	
     257	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     258

     260	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     261	```
     262	
     263	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     264	
     265	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     266	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     267	
     268	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     269	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     270	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     271	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     272	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     273	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     274	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     275	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     276	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     277	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     278	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     279	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     280	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     281	      zero or as healthy.
     282	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     283	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     284	- [ ] Every resource you analysed appears by ID (rule R5a): the `fs-...` behind a storage
     285	      claim, the `i-...` behind a node claim, the `cr-...` behind a capacity claim, the
     286	      cluster name, the log group and stream. This holds for resources you cleared, not just
     287	      the one you blamed.
     288	- [ ] **There is an actual answer.** A verdict or root cause is written down, not just
     289	      evidence. If you ran out of room before finishing, the draft still leads with the
     290	      verdict you can support and marks the rest `Not checked` (rule R1).
     291	
     292	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     293	
     294	## Success criteria
     295	
     296	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     297	  proven coverage.
     298	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     299	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     300	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     301	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     302	- No mutating API call was made.

{"id": "d9bad510-04b4-403c-9720-eab72b4343a3", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_3chdgmirpigCp8MOsVukCE", "content": [{"text": "     1	# NCCL Transport, NVLink / NVSwitch, and EFA Signals
     2	
     3	Where each GPU-communication signal can be seen, what a good and a bad value look like,
     4	and what to do when it is not visible. Log strings are quoted from the sources linked in
     5	each section. Do not paraphrase them into search patterns that match more than they say.
     6	
     7	## 1. Which transport NCCL actually used
     8	
     9	NCCL writes its transport choices only when `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` (or higher) is set, and only
     10	to the job's stdout or to `NCCL_DEBUG_FILE`. These reach CloudWatch only if the customer
     11	ships job output. Search every log source found in SKILL.md Step 3a for `NCCL INFO` and
     12	`NCCL WARN` first. **If there are no NCCL lines at all, NCCL transport is `Not observable`.**
     13	Never infer "NCCL used EFA" from the instance type or the EFA security group.
     14

     34	The CloudWatch agent's NVIDIA plugin does **not** collect any NVLink counter (its full
     35	metric list is utilization, temperature, power, memory, PCIe link, encoder, and clocks).

     116	
     117	`DescribeInstanceTypes` does not report NVSwitch or NVLink. Use the "GPU Peer to Peer"
     118	column of the [EC2 accelerated computing instance page](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/accelerated-computing/),
     119	summarised here as checked:
     120	
     121	| Instance types | GPU peer to peer | Treat as |
     122	|----------------|------------------|----------|
     123	| p4d.24xlarge, p4de.24xlarge | 600 GB/s NVSwitch | NVSwitch |
     124	| p5.48xlarge, p5e.48xlarge, p5en.48xlarge | 900 GB/s NVSwitch | NVSwitch |
     125	| p6-b200.48xlarge, p6-b300.48xlarge, P6e-GB200 UltraServers | 1800 GB/s NVSwitch | NVSwitch (P6e: NVLink domain spans the UltraServer) |
     126	| p5.4xlarge and other single-GPU sizes | N/A | No intra-node GPU communication |
     127	| Multi-GPU g7 and g7e sizes | Yes via PCIe | PCIe peer to peer, no NVSwitch |
     128	| Multi-GPU g4dn, g5, g6, g6e sizes | Not listed | `NVSwitch presence unverified`; do not expect Fabric Manager; the operator checks `nvidia-smi topo -m` |
     129	
     130	For a type not in this table, re-check the instance page. Never infer NVSwitch from the
     131	GPU model name.
     132	
     133	**The number in that table and the number `nvidia-smi` prints are not in the same units.**
     134	On a healthy `p6-b300.48xlarge`, `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows `NV18` between every GPU pair,
     135	meaning 18 bonded NVLinks, and `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` reports `53.125 GB/s` per link. Work
     136	that through and you get 956.25 GB/s in one direction, roughly half the 1800 GB/s listed
     137	above. Nothing is wrong: the published figure counts both directions, while `nvidia-smi`
     138	reports one. Divide one by the other and you will "discover" a half-width fabric on
     139	hardware that is fine. What actually matters is whether the link count and per-link rate
     140	match across the GPUs in the node. An asymmetry between GPUs is worth chasing; a gap
     141	against the published aggregate is not.

     85	## Event timeline (Step 3): Build the event timeline
     86	
     87	Pull all of these for the impact window ±30 minutes, then merge them into one ordered
     88	timeline:
     89	
     90	1. **GPU driver (NVRM) messages, from every log source that has them.** The NVIDIA
     91	   driver writes Xids to the OS system log as `NVRM: Xid (PCI:<bus-id>): <code>, ...`.
     92	   EC2 cannot see them from outside the instance, so they reach CloudWatch Logs only
     93	   if something on the node ships them. Find the source for the orchestrator (see
     94	   **Step 3a** below), then run this Logs Insights query against each source:
     95	
     96	   ```
     97	   fields @timestamp, @logStream, @message
     98	   | filter @message like /NVRM: Xid/
     99	   | sort @timestamp asc
     100	   | limit 200
     101	   ```
     102	
     103	   Extract per Xid: instance (from the stream name or message), code, PCI bus ID, and
     104	   first-occurrence time.
     105	
     106	2. **HyperPod health-monitoring agent (HMA) detections** (HyperPod only). Log group
     107	   `/aws/sagemaker/Clusters/<ClusterName>/<ClusterId>`, per-node log stream
     108	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<instance-group>/<instance-id>`:
     109	
     110	   ```
     111	   fields @timestamp, @logStream, @message
     112	   | filter @message like /HealthMonitoringAgentDetectionEvent/
     113	   | sort @timestamp asc
     114	   ```
     115	
     116	   Extract per event: instance, `reason`, node condition (for example
     117	   `NvidiaErrorReboot`, `NvidiaErrorTerminate`), any `NVRM: Xid (...): <code>` text, and
     118	   DCGM policy violations (`"condition: ":"XID Error"` with `ErrNum`). HMA's own
     119	   `reason` is a strong classification signal: `XidHardwareFailure` points to Branch A,
     120	   while `XidUserAppError` means HMA judged the Xid application-caused and took no node
     121	   action, which points to Branch F.
     122	
     123	3. **Other HyperPod log streams** (HyperPod only) in the same log group, including
     124	   `LifecycleConfig/<instance-group>/<instance-id>` for lifecycle script failures on
     125	   replacement nodes, and any deep health check streams. Filter for `ERROR`, `FAIL`,
     126	   `Xid`, `EFA`, `NCCL`.

     129	   and the region, then `health.DescribeAffectedEntities` for the cluster's instance

     131	   strong signal.

     134	   instance status checks, and scheduled events (`instance-retirement`,
     135	   `system-reboot`, `system-maintenance`).

     141	   `Capacity Block Expiration Warning` event 40 minutes before the end.

{"id": "8ba1c439-e46c-44ab-9a97-1a0b0c13da67", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_syoOpXrnr7AFCIOdiFcBkZ", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Frequent Cluster Edge Cases
     2	
     3	Frequent causes of GPU cluster incidents that are not GPU faults. Each has a read-only
     4	detection path and a fixed conclusion. Log strings are quoted from the linked pages.
     5	
     6	## 1. Subnet IP and network interface exhaustion
     7	
     8	Large GPU instances consume many IP addresses, and a subnet's CIDR cannot be changed later.
     9	HyperPod documents that each P5 instance creates **32 IP addresses on Slurm** (one per
     10	network card) and **81 on EKS** (50 from the primary card plus one from each of the other 31).
     11	HyperPod cannot request the ENI quota increase itself.
     12	
     13	Detect:
     14	- `ec2.DescribeSubnets` `AvailableIpAddressCount` for every subnet in `VpcConfig` and each
     15	  group's `OverrideVpcConfig` (HyperPod), or the cluster's compute subnets.
     16	- IPs per node: HyperPod P5 per the figures above; EC2 nodes: count of `NetworkInterfaces`
     17	  plus their secondary private IPs from `DescribeInstances`.
     18	- `servicequotas.GetServiceQuota` for Amazon VPC `L-DF5E4CA3` (Network interfaces per
     19	  Region) versus network interfaces in use.
     20	
     21	Conclude: in an incident, `CurrentCount < TargetCount` with free IPs below one node's need
     22	is a network capacity cause (Branch B), not hardware. In pre-flight, RISK when free IPs
     23	cannot cover one replacement node.
     24	
     25	Source: [HyperPod prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-prerequisites.html).
     26	
     27	## 2. EFA security group outbound rule
     28	
     29	HyperPod documents: allow all traffic to and from the security group itself, and "avoid
     30	using `0.0.0.0/0` for outbound rules, as this may cause EFA health check failures". Flag an
     31	outbound `0.0.0.0/0` rule on an EFA HyperPod cluster as RISK, and link it to any EFA deep
     32	health check failure. Source: same page.
     33	
     34	## 3. ParallelCluster nodes that never arrive (scaling, bootstrap, protected mode)
     35	
     36	Streams in `/aws/parallelcluster/<cluster>-<timestamp>` on the head node:
     37	`<host>.<instance-id>.clustermgtd`, `.slurm_resume`, `.slurmctld`; on compute nodes
     38	`.cloud-init-output`.
     39	
     40	| String | Meaning | Conclusion |
     41	|--------|---------|------------|
     42	| `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` in `clustermgtd` or `slurm_resume` | EC2 had no capacity for the launch | Branch B (capacity) |
     43	| `Found the following bootstrap failure nodes` | Nodes launched but failed to join | Configuration or lifecycle failure; node verdict LEAVE ALONE; read the node's `cloud-init-output` |
     44	| `Node bootstrap error` | Reason for a bootstrap failure | Same |
     45	| `Partitions bootstrap failure count` ... `cluster will be set into protected mode if protected failure count reach threshold` | Repeated bootstrap failures | After the threshold, the cluster enters protected mode and stops launching into the failing queue. Report the queue |
     46	
     47	Sources: [Slurm cluster protected mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/slurm-protected-mode-v3.html),
     48	[Node bootstrap error](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/compute-node-initialization-bootstrap-error-v3.html).
     49	
     50	## 4. EFA nodes in a public subnet (ParallelCluster)
     51	
     52	From ParallelCluster 3.15.0, EFA-enabled nodes launch with more than one network interface,
     53	and "Amazon EC2 does not auto-assign a public IP address to an instance launched with more
     54	than one network interface". Such nodes "fail to bootstrap if they rely on an auto-assigned
     55	public IP for internet access (a public subnet with no NAT gateway)".
     56	
     57	Detect: compute subnet route table has `0.0.0.0/0` to an `igw-` and no NAT; nodes have more
     58	than one network interface and no `PublicIpAddress`. Conclude: proven precondition FAIL,
     59	node verdict LEAVE ALONE. Source: [ParallelCluster EFA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/efa-v3.html).
     60	
     61	## 5. Capacity Block not yet active
     62	
     63	`DescribeCapacityReservations` `State = scheduled` with `StartDate` in the future: nodes
     64	cannot launch into it yet. Expected behavior, not a fault. State the start time.
     65	
     66	## 6. FSx for Lustre maintenance window
     67	
     68	`fsx.DescribeFileSystems` `WeeklyMaintenanceStartTime` (day and UTC time). During patching
     69	"your file system will be temporarily unavailable", operations retry, and "the in-memory
     70	cache will be erased during maintenance, leading to higher latencies". A stall that starts
     71	inside the window, followed by higher latency, is FSx maintenance: `Proven` if client I/O
     72	drops exactly in the window, otherwise `Hypothesis`.
     73	Source: [FSx for Lustre maintenance windows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/maintenance-windows.html).
     74	
     75	## 7. HyperPod-specific visibility
     76	
     77	- HyperPod "currently doesn't support the exportation of system metrics to Amazon
     78	  CloudWatch", and its instances do not appear in the customer account's EC2 APIs. GPU
     79	  activity for HyperPod nodes is therefore `Not observable` in CloudWatch; point to the
     80	  HyperPod observability add-on (Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus). Source:
     81	  [HyperPod FAQ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-faq-slurm.html).
     82	- Deep health check results are written to `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams in the
     83	  cluster log group, for example `Encountered FaultyInstance. Replace the Instance. ...
     84	  ERROR:Bandwidth has less than threshold: Expected minimum threshold :80,NCCL Test output Bw: 30`.
     85	  A failure there is hardware-grounded evidence for REPLACE.
     86	- HyperPod EKS node labels (read with the EKS API when available):
     87	  `sagemaker.amazonaws.com/node-health-status` = `Schedulable`, `Unschedulable` (deep
     88	  health checks running), `UnschedulablePendingReplacement`, or `UnschedulablePendingReboot`.
     89	  A node can be `Running` in the SageMaker API while tainted unschedulable. With
     90	  `NodeRecovery = None`, a pending label stays until an operator acts.
     91	  Source: [HyperPod EKS resilience labels](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-eks-resiliency-node-labels.html).
     92	
     93	## 8. Straggler GPU (clock, temperature, power, PCIe)
     94	
     95	With `CWAgent` NVIDIA metrics per `index`: `nvidia_smi_clocks_current_sm`,
     96	`nvidia_smi_temperature_gpu`, `nvidia_smi_power_draw`, `nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_current`,
     97	`nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_current`. One GPU clearly below its peers on the same node during
     98	the same job is a straggler candidate: MONITOR, then REBOOT if it persists. Label it
     99	`Hypothesis` unless it lines up with the slowdown; outlier thresholds are heuristics.
     100	AWS recommends persistently setting maximum clocks
     101	([Optimize GPU settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/optimize_gpu.html))."}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_Mx0Vfatak0cE2DsCqQT6CT", "content": [{"text": "{"111122223333": {"LaunchTemplates": []}}"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "user_reference": null}

### Key disambiguation
All non-empty results belong to a **separate HyperPod/EKS environment** (`skilltest-hp-eks`, `skilltest-hyperpod-sg`) that merely shares VPC `vpc-0028c20959269e96f` with our FSx. **None** reference our cluster SGs (sg-085312d23331273ac, sg-0cb46d151d8d7059f), our FSx SG (sg-0c6c57aa6bccdbb0d), our FSx ENIs, our launch template (lt-095390fd0f31d97c6), or stack `distributed-training-triage-b200`.

I therefore could not inspect commits or pipeline runs for training-config changes (batch size, dataloader workers, prefetch, NCCL/EFA env vars, FSx mount options). **No code-integration deployment data is available for this environment.**

**No "Proven" and no "Hypothesis" change could be attributed to our cluster or FSx.** This is a clear negative finding: within this scope and window, infrastructure configuration and deployment activity do **not** explain the throughput drop.

     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
