     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     104	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     105	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     106	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     107	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     108	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     109	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     110	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     111	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     112	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     113	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     114	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     115	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     116	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     117	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     118	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     119	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     120	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     121	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     122	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     123	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     124	R11. **When the logs are dead, ask the control plane.** On a HyperPod cluster with
     125	   `NodeProvisioningMode = Continuous`, `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` gives you a node and
     126	   cluster timeline that owes nothing to a log agent, so it keeps answering when a stream has
     127	   gone silent or a node has disappeared. Filter the window with `EventTimeAfter` and
     128	   `EventTimeBefore`, narrow with `NodeId` or `InstanceGroupName`, sort with
     129	   `SortBy=EventTime`, and page through `NextToken`. Where a `Description` is not
     130	   self-explanatory, `DescribeClusterEvent` has the detail. Note that the response has no
     131	   severity or level field at all, so any grouping you apply is your own and should be
     132	   described that way. If `NodeProvisioningMode` is anything other than `Continuous` the call
     133	   is not supported; write `ListClusterEvents not supported` in the coverage table and carry
     134	   on. What you must not do is report a dead log as "no events" without either trying this
     135	   source or saying it was unavailable.
     136	
     137	## Pick the mode
     138	
     139	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     140	|---------------|------|--------------|
     141	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     142	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     143	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     144	
     145	## Workflow checklist
     146	
     147	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     148	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     149	
     150	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request: account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     151	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     152	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     153	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     154	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     155	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     156	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     157	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     158	
     159	## Step 1: Scope
     160	
     161	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     162	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     163	
     164	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     165	
     166	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     167	inventory API calls and the eight timeline sources, and
     168	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     169	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     170	
     171	```
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     173	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     174	```
     175	
     176	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     177	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     178	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     179	
     180	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     181	
     182	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     183	and hourly coverage queries, and
     184	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     185	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     186	
     187	```
     188	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     189	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     190	```
     191	
     192	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     193	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     194	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     195	groups you searched and that none did.
     196	
     197	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     198	
     199	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     200	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     201	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     202	
     203	```
     204	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     205	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     206	```
     207	
     208	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     209	
     210	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     211	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     212	
     213	```
     214	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     215	```
     216	
     217	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     218	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     219	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     220	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     221	actions only.
     222	
     223	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     224	
     225	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     226	
     227	```
     228	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     229	```
     230	
     231	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     232	Steps 4 and 5.

{"id": "39045910-9149-4ff8-a22d-da3142008bce", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_y8WrE8UkVDdIZGOBUxMOM9", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.3"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass, and always leave room to answer.** In chat, do not stop to ask a
     34	   question and do not hand off to a separate investigation before answering. If an input is
     35	   missing, use the default (impact window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and
     36	   72 hours), state the assumption, and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or
     37	   performance questions with no time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only
     38	   after the answer.
     39	   **Budget the evidence gathering so the answer always gets written.** An investigation that
     40	   runs out of room before it reports is worth nothing to the operator, and it is worse than a
     41	   partial answer because it looks like a failure rather than a finding. So: collect the
     42	   mandatory evidence for the mode first (R2, R4, R5, and for Mode P the P1 to P6 core), then
     43	   write the report. Pick up the optional checks only with what is left. If you notice you are
     44	   deep into tool calls and have not yet produced an answer, **stop collecting and report what
     45	   you have**, marking everything unreached as `Not checked` with the call that would close
     46	   it. Never end a turn with evidence gathered and no verdict.
     47	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     48	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). Read `NodeProvisioningMode` from `DescribeCluster`: if it is
     49	   `Continuous`, also pull `sagemaker.ListClusterEvents` for the window (see rule R11), which
     50	   is the only timeline source that survives broken log delivery. On any other value the call
     51	   is unsupported and must be skipped, not retried.
     52	   EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     53	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     54	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     55	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     56	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     57	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     58	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     59	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     60	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     61	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     62	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     63	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     64	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     65	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     66	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     67	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     68	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     69	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     70	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     71	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     72	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     73	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     74	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     75	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     76	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     77	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     78	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     79	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     80	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     81	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     82	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     83	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     84	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     85	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     86	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     87	R5a. **Name every resource you looked at, by ID.** A finding the operator cannot re-run is
     88	   not a finding. Whatever you analysed, put its identifier in the answer: the FSx file system
     89	   (`fs-...`) behind any storage claim, the instance IDs (`i-...`) behind any node claim, the
     90	   cluster name, the capacity reservation (`cr-...`) behind any capacity claim, and the log
     91	   group and stream behind any log claim as R5 already requires. "The file system was
     92	   saturated" or "the metrics looked fine" names nothing and cannot be checked. This applies
     93	   to the resource you cleared as much as the one you blamed, since ruling something out is
     94	   only useful if the reader knows what was ruled out.
     95	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     96	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     97	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     98	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     99	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     100	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     101	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     102	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     103	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
